title: A Novel Bioreactor for High Density Cultivation of Diverse Microbial Communities
protocol: Arrange the reactor components according to the schematic in Figure 1.
Place the reactor (R) on a mixing plate and add a stir bar to the reactor.
Place the recycle tank (RT) beside the stir plate and reactor so that the effluent (top) port of the tank is directed towards the edge of the lab bench.
Place the waste container (W) underneath the effluent (top) port of the recycle tank (RT).
Place the feed tank (FT) next to the recycle tank (RT).
Secure the reactor (R) against tipping with an appropriately sized stand and clamp.
Secure the recycle tank (RT) to prevent movement.
Insert neoprene peristaltic pump tubing in the recycle (Pump A) and feed (Pump B) pump heads.
Install the pump heads onto the pump drives with the screws provided with the pump drives.
Connect Pump A's tubing to the ports on the reactor and the recycle tank.
Insert the end of Pump B's tubing into the feed tank and the recycle tank.
Connect the top reactor port to the recycle tank with tubing.
Apply clamps to the tubing at the reactor ports.
Prepare the mineral stock solution.
Add 200 g sodium bicarbonate to a 1 L volumetric flask with 500 ml deionized water.

Add 40 g monobasic potassium phosphate, 4 g magnesium sulfate, 4 g ferric chloride, 4 g calcium chloride, 1 g copper chloride, 1 g cobalt chloride hexahydrate, and 1 g nickel chloride hexahydrate to the flask.
Swirl forcefully to encourage dissolution of salts.
Add an additional 400 ml deionized water after complete dissolution of salts.
Add deionized water to bring the total volume of mineral stock solution to 1 L.
Prepare the ammonia stock solution.
Dissolve 38.214 grams of ammonium chloride in approximately 900 ml deionized water.
Add deionized water to bring the total volume up to 1,000 ml.
Prepare the nitrate stock solution.
Dissolve 72.413 g of potassium nitrate in approximately 900 ml deionized water.
Add deionized water to bring the total volume up to 1,000 ml.
Prepare feed/influent solution by diluting 2 ml of ammonia stock solution to a total volume of 1 L.
Add 0.5 ml mineral solution per liter of feed solution being prepared.
Dilute 2 ml of nitrate stock solution to a total volume of 1 L and add 0.5 ml mineral solution.
Prepare a total of 5 L of influent for starting the reactor.
Collect at least 10 L of water from an algae-containing water body.
Allow collected water samples to settle undisturbed for 24 hours.
Decant and discard clear water, leaving concentrated algae suspension in sample bottles.
Combine algae suspensions from all samples into one container.
Repeat settling and decanting steps with combined algae suspension.
Dry a paper vacuum filter (0.45 µm MCE) and aluminum weigh boat overnight at 103 °C.
Cool down dried filter and weigh boat in a desiccator for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Measure the mass of dried filter and weigh boat.
Vacuum filter 20 ml of concentrated algae suspension using dried filter and weigh boat.
Return used filter and weigh boat to oven overnight to dry.
Measure the combined mass of dried filter and weigh boat after filtering algae suspension.
Calculate biomass density within the concentrated algae sample.
Add 750 ml of feed solution to the reactor.
Fill the recycle tank with 500 ml of feed solution.
Use a long pipette to gently add an inoculate suspension containing 1.5 g of algae near the bottom of the reactor.
Allow the inoculum to settle to the bottom of the reactor, ensuring it is settled before proceeding.
Remove the tube clamps and turn on Pump A to a slow flow rate (10 revolutions min-1/38 ml min-1).
Squeeze the tubing to ensure that all air has been expelled.
Gradually add feed solution to the recycle tank as the solution is pumped into the reactor until effluent starts to exit the recycle tank via the top port.
Pour the remaining feed solution into the feed tank.
Set the recycle pump (Pump A) to 19 revolutions min-1, establishing a recycle flow rate of 72.5 ml min-1.
Observe the algae begin to loft from the bottom of the reactor.
Determine the algae biomass zone height using the gradations on the reactor.
Ensure that the height is constant before proceeding to the next step.
Turn on the mixing plate at very low speed; a setting of 1 or 2 is appropriate to start.
Set mixing speed to establish a clear algae boundary within the reactor (approximately 10-15 cm in height).
Start the feed pump after observing a clear boundary between the algal plug and the reactor fluid.
Set the pump to 25 revolutions min-1, establishing a flow rate of 1.5 ml min-1.
Observe the reactor fluid exit the effluent port due to gravity and displacement caused by the incoming influent stream.
Collect 20 ml of effluent samples daily from within the recycle tank.
Collect 20 ml of influent samples daily directly from the feed tank.
Vacuum filter samples to remove suspended solids prior to storage and analysis.
Store the influent and effluent samples at -20 °C until further analysis.
